analysis:
The change is documentation-only in docs/reference/configuration.md (head 393-395). The visible patch swaps a DARKBLOOM_CBV2_SOLO_PREFILL_STRIPE row for DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the new row's full text and any later changes are not visible. The two units show only the base lines 520-687 and the head lines 1-353. The head excerpt does not reach line 393, so the changed lines cannot be cited or checked on either side. The unseen patch tail is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety.

What I examined: the surrounding documented security-relevant controls, none of which changed in this diff.
- The prefix-cache environment variables (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE, the SSD TTL capped at 1800 seconds, the disk budget, the debug key file, the ephemeral and test-root controls).
- The cache.directory and cache.volume_uuid validation.
- The App Attest worker qualification flags, which use exact `1` and are described as creating no local trust.
- The endpoint-resumption and logout documentation.

These are consistent with the T-041 (TTL 30 minutes, DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch, debug key file DEBUG-only) and TB-011 / T-053 descriptions in the canonical model. Only the first 7 text lines of the base unit were cross-checked against T-041's TTL and DBK3 claims, and they matched. I found no weakening of a security default, no new forwarded environment variable and no new attack surface in the visible text.

Open question for integration: confirm that the PREFILL_CHUNK row and any other hunks in the truncated patch do not alter the LaunchAgent passthrough claims. The row should be a performance knob only. Whether it interacts with the prefix cache or the memory-admission guards (T-028 / T-029) is unverified.
